tasks.given: A burning carbon-electrode arc; compare rapid cooling of the negative rod with cooling the positive rod.
tasks.independent_solution: In the ordinary hot-cathode DC carbon-arc explanation, the negative electrode supplies emitted electrons. Strong cathode cooling reduces thermionic supply sharply; if it can no longer sustain the required discharge current, the arc weakens and may extinguish. The positive anode primarily collects the electrons, so cooling it is not the same direct interruption of cathode thermionic emission. This does not imply that anode cooling has no effect: electrode heat balance, gas/plasma conditions and circuit response are coupled. Without final temperatures and operating conditions the source does not fix an exact transient or guarantee identical behavior in every arc regime.
requiredBoundaries: Explicitly identify the ordinary heated-cathode model; do not claim every arc is exclusively thermionic.
Do not call the positive anode the principal source of those cathode-emitted electrons.
State the emission-supply condition if predicting extinction, rather than guaranteeing every arbitrarily small cooling extinguishes the arc.
Do not say anode cooling can never influence stability, current or cathode temperature.
Do not invent current, voltage, cooling temperature, arc length, emission rate or observed transient.
tasks.scopeHOLD: Unconditional exact extinction/no-effect prediction for unspecified thermal and circuit conditions is not established by the source; a qualified ordinary-model explanation can still be reviewed.

tasks.given: The source states that a candle flame between charged capacitor plates bends toward the negative electrode; explain that observation.
tasks.independent_solution: Combustion supplies charge carriers in the flame, including positive ions and negative carriers. The electric field acts on them; collisional momentum transfer to the neutral gas produces electrohydrodynamic motion. Positive ions are driven toward the negative electrode, while electrons and negative ions have the opposite electric-force direction. The stated cathode-directed bending is consistent with the net field-driven force/flow asymmetry in that observed configuration, not with every neutral gas molecule directly feeling the same electric force. The source does not supply the carrier distributions or flow field needed to derive a quantitative universal one-way wind. Flame bending and the detailed ionic-wind directions must not be equated, and the entire flame need not be declared a uniformly positively charged body.
requiredBoundaries: Explain charged-species electric force and collisional gas momentum transfer, not simple magnetic attraction or unqualified heating attraction.
Do not erase electrons or negative ions or say that all flame particles are positive.
Do not claim every flame or all local ionic wind always flows only toward the cathode.
Preserve the source's stated negative-electrode bending without inventing field strength, voltage, carrier density, temperature, force or a measured wind speed.
A jet-flame study may constrain an overbroad mechanism claim; it is not experimental proof of this source candle geometry.
tasks.scopeHOLD: Quantitative carrier/force attribution and universal directional prediction remain underdetermined; the stated qualitative observation is not itself a blanket HOLD.

primaryReferenceLimitChecks.readMethod: cloak-fetch, rendered abstract and bibliographic record only
primaryReferenceLimitChecks.observation: The authors model coupled plasma/electrode heat and current transport, electron emission/absorption and electrode surface processes. Anode heat balance matters to spot formation. This supports retaining anode thermal-coupling limits, not a claim that any anode cooling is irrelevant.

primaryReferenceLimitChecks.title: Visualization of ionic wind in laminar jet flames
primaryReferenceLimitChecks.authors: D. G. Park, S. H. Chung, M. S. Cha
primaryReferenceLimitChecks.readMethod: cloak-fetch, authors' university repository abstract and bibliographic record
primaryReferenceLimitChecks.observation: The experiments relate flame response to electric body force on charge-carrying species. In the tested jet arrangements lower-potential flame skewing coexists with ionic wind toward both electrodes. This rules out using visible flame deflection alone to declare every local gas flow cathode-directed; it does not establish a quantitative result for the textbook candle.
